description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual salary using a 38-hour week and 52-week year. Includes tax, super, and references to the nsw teacher salary 2025 pdf.
salarySummary: For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52, before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week (typically 38 for full-time) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $30/hour × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year. This is your gross annual pay before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of leave entitlements. On the timesheet, you enter your base rate and check the casual loading box; the calculator adds 25%. Do not enter a rate that already includes loading.

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary by your employer. For example, if your annual salary is $60,000, your employer contributes an additional $7,200 to your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

When you have an hourly rate or a salary offer, understanding the annual equivalent helps you compare jobs and plan your finances. The standard method is to multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week and then by 52 weeks in a year. For full-time employees, the typical week is 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. So the formula is:

**Annual gross pay ≈ hourly rate × 38 hours per week × 52 weeks**

This gives you the gross annual salary before tax, super, and any deductions. It assumes you work the same hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. If you work part-time or different hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly.

### The Fortnightly View

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly pay by two. For example, if your weekly pay is $1,000 (based on $26.32/hour × 38 hours), your fortnightly pay is $2,000. This can help you budget and compare with salary offers that are quoted fortnightly. Our [the timesheet](/) shows both weekly and fortnightly amounts automatically.

### Using the Timesheet

Our timesheet (the home page) lets you enter your base hourly rate. If you are a casual employee, you can check the box to add 25% casual loading on top of that base rate. **Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading**; the calculator applies it correctly. The timesheet then shows your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay, plus estimated tax and super. It's a quick way to see the numbers.

## Understanding Key Pay Concepts

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. However, many industries have award rates that are higher. For example, teachers are covered by the Educational Services (Teachers) Award 2020, which sets minimum rates based on classification and experience. The NSW Department of Education publishes a detailed salary schedule, often in a PDF format – you may have seen the **nsw teacher salary 2025 pdf** that outlines incremental steps. That document is the authoritative source for teacher pay in NSW public schools. Note that those rates are specific to the award and are not the same as the average earnings for all NSW workers.

### Average Weekly Earnings vs. Your Pay

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports Average Weekly Earnings (AWE). For May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings in New South Wales averaged $2,108.80 per week. This is an average across all industries and occupations, not a median for any specific job like teaching. Your individual pay may be higher or lower depending on your role, experience, and location. For a more tailored comparison, refer to award rates or your enterprise agreement. You can find more data on our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page.

### Superannuation (Super)

Super guarantee is currently 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. It is not deducted from your gross pay. For example, if your annual salary is $70,000, your employer contributes an additional $8,400 to your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. You can learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) on our site.

### Tax and Medicare

The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) sets the resident tax rates for 2026–27:

- Nil tax on income up to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Most residents also pay a Medicare levy of 2% of taxable income. The tax-free threshold and Medicare reduction thresholds apply. Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator uses these rates to estimate your net pay after tax and Medicare.

## Example: Converting a Teacher's Hourly Rate

Suppose a teacher on the NSW salary schedule has a base hourly rate of $45 per hour (this is illustrative; actual rates depend on the award). Working 38 hours per week, the annual gross pay would be:

$45 × 38 × 52 = $88,920 per year

If the teacher is casual, the base rate might be $45, and with 25% loading it becomes $56.25 per hour. The annual gross would then be $56.25 × 38 × 52 = $111,150. However, casual teachers may not work every week of the year, so actual annual earnings could be lower.

Remember that the **nsw teacher salary 2025 pdf** provides the official rates for permanent and temporary teachers. Those rates are set by the NSW Department of Education and are updated periodically. Always check the latest PDF for accurate figures.

### How to Find Your Correct Rate

If you are a teacher in NSW, start by locating the current salary schedule. The NSW Department of Education releases a PDF each year, often titled something like "nsw teacher salary 2025 pdf". This document lists step increments based on years of service and qualifications. For example, a graduate teacher might start at a lower step, while an experienced teacher with a master's degree may be on a higher step. Your award or enterprise agreement may also specify allowances for leadership roles or remote work. For other industries, check the Fair Work Ombudsman's [pay guides](/blog) or use our [reference tables](/data) for award rates.

## Important Considerations

- **Penalty rates and allowances** are not included in this simple conversion. If you work weekends, nights, or overtime, your actual pay will be higher.
- **Salary sacrifice** arrangements can reduce your taxable income but are not accounted for here.
- **HELP loans** and the Medicare levy surcharge are not deducted in our estimates.
- The formula assumes 52 weeks of work. If you take unpaid leave, your annual pay will be less.
- **Casual loading** is an extra 25% on the base rate, but casual employees do not receive paid leave. The loading compensates for that. Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains more.

For a more detailed breakdown, visit our [reference tables](/data) which include award rates and other benchmarks.

## Disclaimer

The annual pay shown here is an estimate: hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
